questions.question: **In the following question, four words are given out of which one word is correctly spelt. Select the correctly spelt word.**
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is** Proximate**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**:-

 
• 'Proximate' derives from Latin **'proximatus' **itself the past participle of the verb **'proximare' **meaning** 'to approach'**.
 
• Let's look at the **correct spelling** and **meaning** of the given word:-
 
 
• **Proximate***(adjective) -*(especially of the cause of something) closest in relationship; immediate.
 
• For Example - The fact that a storm may show up the poor condition of a flat roof does not signify that storm was the** proximate** cause of damage to it.
 
 

**Therefore, the correct spelling of the given word is** *Proximate*.

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

A nation’s progress

A-requires many policies, many

B-on many fronts

C-plans, and actions
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is** ACB**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**:-

 
• The first sentence in the sequence should be** A** because no other sentence fits in other than A.
 
• The second sentence should be** C **because** 'many' **cannot be followed by **'on'** as it will be erroneous.
 
• The third sentence should be** B**.
 
• This sequence tells us **what is required for the progress of a nation**.
 
• No other sequence can convey this meaning.

**Therefore, the correct sequence for the given paragraph is*** ACB*.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

Nothing (have prepared) him for a continent that was a country, and a land of terrific complexity.
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is **Had prepared**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**:-

 
• In the above given sentence,** 'had prepared' **will be used.
 
• It is so because the sentence is **past perfect tense**.
 
• In past perfect tense we follow the given structure:-
 
 
• Structure -** Subject + had + V₃ + Object.**
 
• For Example - He **had left** for India.
 
 
 
• Therefore, we use **V₃ **form of the verb with 'had'.
 
• Here in the given options, option 1 is invalid because we do not use** V₁ form of the verb** with** 'had'**.
 
• Option 3 is incorrect because we do not use** present participle form of the verb **with **'had'**.
 
• **'Have prepared' **is incorrect because the sentence is in past perfect tense(an action which has completed a long time ago).

**Therefore, the correct sentence will be** *Nothing **had prepared **him for a continent that was a country, and a land of terrific complexity.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**:-

• In past perfect tense we follow the given structure:-
 
 
• Structure - Subject + had + V3 + Object.
 
• For Example - He had left for India.

• The only option which contains the **V₃** form of the verb with **'had'** is option 2.

• **'Have reversed'** cannot be used because **'situation'** is a **singular noun **and we cannot use** 'have'** with a **singular noun**.

**Therefore, the correct sentence is** *I could see that the situation **had reversed*****.**

questions.question: Be it the citizens ________ the country
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is** Of.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**:-

 
• In the above given blank,** 'of'** will be used.
 
• It is so because citizens **belong** to the country.
 
• Therefore the preposition '**of**' must be used.
 
• **'Of'** is a preposition which is used to denote relation.
 
 
• For Example - Adarsh is a friend** of** mine.
 
 
 
• The other options are **irrelevant** because of the following reasons:-
 
 
• **'Off' **is used to denote **separation**.
 
 
• For Example - He fell of the train.
 
 
 
• **'From'** is used to denote **a point of time/distance at which something starts and then continues. **It is also used to denote **separation**.
 
 
• For Examples- The price of petrol will rise by Rs. 2 **from** Sunday.
 
 
 
• **'For' **is used to denote how long something lasts.
 
 
• For Example - David was on leave **for** 5 days.
 
 
 
 

**Therefore, the correct answer to the blank is*** Of*.

questions.question: India, perceived ________ in the distribution

Here the correct answer is **Fairness.**

• We should use the noun** 'fairness' **here.
 
• It is so because **'perceived fairness'** has been used as** one single term** in this sentence that conveys **one idea**.
 
• **'Perceptions of fairness' **refer to any element of the environment perceived by individuals or collectives as fair according to previous norms or standards.
 
• On the other hand **'perceived duty',** **'perceived faith'** doesn't make sense whereas** 'perceived fairness' **is a broad concept related to **employee welfare.**

**Therefore, the correct answer for the blank is** *Fairness*

questions.question: Encouraged in a ________ environment.
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is **Capitalistic**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**:-

 
• Here we must use an** adjective**, because** 'environment'** is a **noun**.
 
• Adjectives are words that describe the qualities or states of being of nouns such as *enormous, doglike, silly, yellow, fun, fast*. 
 
• They can also describe the quantity of nouns such as *many, few, millions, eleven*.
 
• **'Capitalism'** cannot be used because it is a **noun** meaning an economic and political system in which a country's trade and industry are controlled by private owners for profit, rather than by the state.
 
• **'Capital'** cannot be used because it is also a** noun** meaning wealth in the form of money or other assets owned by a person or organization or available for a purpose such as starting a company or investing.
 
• **'Capitalization'** is invalid because it is also a** noun **meaning the provision of capital for a company, or the conversion of income or assets into capital.

**Therefore, the correct answer for the blank is** *Capitalistic*.

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect Speech. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct Speech.**

“German is easy to teach”, she said.

options.text: She told us that German was easy to teach.
She informed German was easy to teach.
She said that German was easy to teach.

questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is **She said that German was easy to teach**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**:-

__
 
• Let's look at the steps for changing the sentence from direct to indirect speech:

 
 
• As the reporting verb is in the past tense and direct speech is in the** simple present** tense, we will take the following steps:-
 
• The conjunction 'that' is used in place of the comma and the inverted comma are removed.
 
• The simple present tense (is easy) is changed to **simple **past tense (was easy) in the direct speech.
 
 

**Therefore, the correct indirect speech pf the given direct speech is** ***She said that German was easy to teach.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 *The following table will enable us to know how tense changes in indirect speech:-

 
 

 Direct Speech
 Indirect Speech
 
 

 Simple Present* (Subject + V1 + Object)*
 Simple Past* (Subject + V2 + Object)*
 
 

 Present Continuous *(Subject + is/am/are + V1 + ing + Object)*
 Past Continuous *(Subject + was/were + V1 + ing + Object)*
 
 

 Present Perfect *(Subject + has/have + V3 + Object)*
 Past Perfect* (Subject + had + V3 + Object)*
 
 

 Simple Past* (Subject + V2 + Object)*
 Past Perfect *(Subject + had + V3 + Object)*
 
 

 Past Continuous *(Subject + was/were + V1 + ing + Object)*
 Past Perfect Continuous* (Subject + had been + V1 + ing + Object)*
 
 

 Simple Future *(Subject + will/shall + V1 + Object)*
 Present Conditional *(Subject + would + V1 +Object)*
 
 

 Future Continuous *(Subject + will/shall + V1 + ing + Object)*
 Conditional Continuous *(Subject + would + be + V1 + ing + Object)*

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice.**

Somebody has stolen my register.

options.text: My register has been stolen upon.
My register has stolen by somebody.
My register has been a steal.

questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is **My register has been stolen.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**:-

__
 
• The given sentence is in **active voice**.
 
• The active voice is in **present perfect tense**.
 
• Whenever an active voice is given in present perfect tense, we change it according to the following structure:-
 
 
• Active Voice -** Subject + has/have + V₃ + Object.**
 
• Passive Voice - **Object + has/have + been + V₃ + Subject.**
 
 
 
• **For Example:-**
 
 
• Active Voice - This man **has washed** the clothes.
 
• Passive Voice - The clothes **have been washed** by this man.
 
 
 
• Here,** 'this man'**(i.e. the subject) has become the object and the **'clothes'**(i.e. the object has become the subject).
 
• In the question sentence **'my register' **is the object and** 'somebody'** is the subject.
 
• Therefore,** 'my register' **has become the subject and** 'somebody'** has become the object.

**Thus, the correct passive voice of the given active voice is** *My register has been stolen.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When we convert active voice to passive voice, three things need to be kept in mind:-

 
 
• Change object into subject.
 
• Change subject into object.
 
• Always use third form of verb in passive voice.
 
• Use 'by' before the new object.

**Therefore, the correct sequence of the sentence will be** *QPR.*
